solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Delicate shot dealing with service when returning

indicators.note: coming back means read the pieces right to left

blocks.note: a go = a shot, an attempt

explanation.surface: A tennis player plays a soft drop shot off a returned serve.
explanation.walkthrough: The tennis words shot, service and returning all do other jobs: service is the church kind, and only the last two pieces turn round.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossamer, as an adjective, describes anything as fine and delicate as a spider's thread.

clue.text: If heard, a dog can be found

indicators.note: tells you to go by the sound of the words

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A remark that a dog will turn up if you listen for it.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, 'a cur' runs together as the verb OCCUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that occurs somewhere can be found there, as in 'the plant occurs in bogs'.

clue.text: Mute used by violinist, otherwise racket pierces terribly

indicators.note: the first pieces go through the middle of the last one

blocks.note: so = terribly, as in 'so sorry'; split S…O around the rest

explanation.surface: A complaint that a violinist's racket is painful even with the mute on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' looks like it describes the noise, but it is an intensifier. A sordino is the Italian name for the clip-on mute.
explanation.definitionFit: Sordino is the musical term for a mute placed on the bridge of a violin.

clue.text: Soaking allotment opened by official staff

indicators.note: the second piece comes first, opening the word

blocks.note: a mace is the ceremonial staff carried before an official
a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: A council allotment gets flooded when the staff open it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Allotment' suggests a vegetable plot and 'staff' employees, but they are a RATION and the MACE carried by a mayor.
explanation.definitionFit: Maceration is softening something by soaking it in liquid.

clue.text: Toss / sticks at the seaside

blocks.note: a verb: to toss about, as a boat in waves
a hard candy sold in sticks at British holiday resorts

explanation.walkthrough: Seaside rock is a stick of hard, brightly coloured candy sold at British holiday resorts, often with the town's name running through it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship tossed on the sea rocks, and rock itself comes in sticks at the seaside.

clue.text: Show contempt for playwright copying Psmith?

blocks.note: Psmith is SMITH with a silent P put in front

explanation.surface: A question whether a playwright borrowing Wodehouse's affectation deserves scorn.
explanation.walkthrough: Psmith, a P. G. Wodehouse character, added a silent P to his plain name Smith; do the same to SHAW.
explanation.definitionFit: Pshaw is an exclamation of contempt, and as a verb means to express that contempt.

clue.text: Innkeeper’s yearly drink cut by doctor

indicators.note: the doctor cuts into the other letters, sitting inside them

blocks.note: one = a drink, as in 'one for the road'

explanation.surface: A landlord's annual tipple is rationed on doctor's orders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink' as a noun, as in 'fancy one?' or 'one for the road'. Padrone is Italian for a landlord or master.
explanation.definitionFit: A padrone is the owner of an Italian inn or hotel.

clue.text: Note struggle behind house, result of shooting there?

indicators.note: the struggle comes after the rest

blocks.note: HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: A fight behind a house leaves the aftermath of a shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooting' reads as gunfire at a crime scene; it is filming, and 'there' points back to the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting here is filming, and a film made in your own house by amateurs is the result; 'there' ties the definition back to the house.

clue.text: Unfriendly judge goes after successful outcome

indicators.note: the judge's word follows the other piece

blocks.note: to try a case is to judge it

explanation.surface: A judge turns hostile after losing the verdict he wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: The judge is a verb here: courts TRY cases.
explanation.definitionFit: A wintry smile or manner is cold and unfriendly.

clue.text: Undesirable growth of plant factory justified in report

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so go by sound

blocks.note: a mill is a plant or factory; due = justified, deserved

explanation.surface: A report describes a factory's plant growth as unwelcome but deserved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' tempts toward greenery, but 'plant factory' is a single industrial MILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Mildew is a fungus that grows where you do not want it.

clue.text: Former South American king provided for driver

blocks.note: the Incas were the pre-Columbian people of Peru

explanation.surface: An Inca king is supplied with a chauffeur.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an adjective phrase: in-car entertainment is provided for the driver.
explanation.definitionFit: In-car things, like a satnav, are for the driver's use.

clue.text: Bad spirit more or less reflected a lack of claret

indicators.note: a mirror image, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: no Médoc: Médoc is a claret, a red Bordeaux

explanation.surface: Someone is in a foul mood, roughly speaking, because the claret has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad spirit' looks like a grumpy mood or a poor wine; it is a demon. Médoc is a Bordeaux region whose red wine is claret.
explanation.definitionFit: A cacodemon is an evil spirit, from Greek kakos, bad.

clue.text: Mistake during dive, leaving five engineers behind

indicators.note: the mistake happens in the middle of the dive
the five goes out of the word

blocks.note: DIVE without V, the Roman five; split D…IE
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A diver fumbles, and five engineers are left behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' reads as left in the rear; it is the definition, a noun for the backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Derriere, from French, is a polite word for the behind.

clue.text: Daughter first mentioned unopened window

indicators.note: the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: FORMER (first mentioned) without its first letter

explanation.surface: A girl was the first to mention the window left shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The former' is the first of two things mentioned; take its F away.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormer is a window set upright in a sloping roof.

clue.text: Ring sailor in race that’s lost time — he’ll protest

indicators.note: the sailor's word drops the time letter

blocks.note: to ring = to bell, give someone a ring

blocks.clueFragment: sailor in race that’s lost time
blocks.note: YACHTER (a sailor in a race) without T, time

explanation.surface: A sailor beaten in a race phones in a complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: The sailor is not the usual AB or TAR: the phrase 'sailor in race' gives the whole word YACHTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bellyacher is a chronic complainer, one who will always protest.

clue.text: Frankly weird present heralded by hearts on card

indicators.note: the hearts-and-card piece comes before the rest
in an across clue, hearts go after the card

blocks.note: a card is a joker, a wit
to serve = to present, as a dish

explanation.surface: A card-game player frankly finds a hand led with hearts a strange gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card' and 'hearts' belong to a pack of cards, but card here is a witty person, a WIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve is restraint in speech, so talking with none held back is talking frankly; an adverb phrase for an adverb.

clue.text: Thin cleaner not thin enough to fit around piano

indicators.note: the phrase goes round the piano

explanation.surface: A slim cleaning tool is still too fat to get round the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thin' appears twice to pull opposite ways: a thin tool, and a phrase meaning its opposite, TOO THICK.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothpick is a thin stick for cleaning between the teeth.

clue.text: Silly wet males not for Germaine Greer, say

indicators.note: a silly arrangement is a mixed-up one

explanation.surface: A jibe that the feminist Germaine Greer has no time for feeble men.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface fits Greer's feminism perfectly, which hides that she is the definition as an example of a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Germaine Greer, author of The Female Eunuch, is a noted woman of letters.

clue.text: Prisoner with muscles died gripping that bunk

indicators.note: the muscles and died hold the prisoner inside

explanation.surface: A muscular convict dies clinging to his prison bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bunk' looks like a prison bed; it is the verb, as in 'do a bunk', meaning run off.
explanation.definitionFit: To bunk or do a bunk is British slang for running away, the same as abscond.

clue.text: Number one hit, of course?

blocks.note: reads as a chart-topping record; meant as the first stroke played
reads as 'naturally'; meant as on a golf course

explanation.surface: A chart-topping song that was bound to succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one hit' reads as a chart-topper and 'of course' as naturally; both are golf, the first shot struck on a course.
explanation.definitionFit: The tee shot is a golfer's first hit on each hole.

clue.text: Hasty dairy supplier not quite filling tin

indicators.note: something not quite complete stops just short, so the word loses its final letter
a filling sits inside something, so the shortened udder goes inside the tin

blocks.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin; split S…N
UDDER, the cow's milk supply, without its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone rushes to fill a tin from a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: The dairy supplier is not a milkman but the cow's UDDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe something done quickly and without warning or thought.

clue.text: Real man using lasso under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue, the man sits below the pressure

explanation.surface: A genuine cowboy stays cool with a lasso under stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Real man' reads as a unit, but Real is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A proper job or a real job: both mean genuine.

clue.text: Work over there has Hebe in the middle

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words

explanation.surface: A painting or poem over there shows the goddess Hebe at its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' looks like a noun, an artwork; with 'over' it is a verb for rehashing.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehash old material is to work it over again.

clue.text: Presume Spooner’s cook specially shaped dish?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the first sounds of words

blocks.note: bake = cook; a mould is a shaped dish, as for jelly

explanation.surface: A guess about what Spooner's cook will serve in a fancy dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of BAKE and MOULD.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'may I make so bold as to ask' means 'may I presume to ask', taking a liberty.

clue.text: Prison officers were kept in by delay

blocks.note: of = by, as in 'the plays of Shakespeare'

explanation.surface: Prison officers had to stay late because of a delay.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the officers the warders; they are the inmates. An Oflag was a German prisoner-of-war camp for officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Oflag, short for Offizierslager, was a German camp where captured officers were held.

clue.text: Something for the offertory when in church?

indicators.note: the word for when goes inside church

blocks.note: as = when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A question about what goes in the collection plate at church.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a churchgoer's question, and the wordplay answers it with 'when' placed in church.
explanation.definitionFit: The offertory is the collection of money during a church service.

clue.text: Learning lover’s posh but heartless, fancy him a lot

indicators.note: take out the middle letters
a fancy arrangement is a rearranged one

explanation.surface: A swot's girlfriend is well-bred but cold, yet fancies him madly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lover' and 'fancy' suggest romance; fancy is the anagram instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek roots philo- (loving) and math- (learning) translate straight into the definition.

clue.text: Very hearty sandwiches to cut into triangles?

indicators.note: the hearty word holds the very letter between its parts

explanation.surface: Instructions for serving generous sandwiches in triangles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' is the verb, not the food; the question mark flags that cutting a sandwich diagonally is just one way to halve.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting a square sandwich corner to corner halves it into two triangles.

clue.text: Assigned to classes, letting name go on a list

indicators.note: with 'go', the name is let out of the word
completes 'letting go', dropping the letter

blocks.clueFragment: Assigned to classes, letting name go

explanation.surface: Pupils are sorted into classes and dropped from the register.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' reads as a register, but it is a ship's lean, and a raked stage or mast is sloped.
explanation.definitionFit: A list is a tilt, so something raked is set at a slant, on a list.

clue.text: One man’s retreat out of Moscow, primarily the stuff of history

indicators.note: something taken out of a place is removed from it, so M comes out of the retreat
primarily means first of all, so only Moscow's first letter is used

blocks.note: a hermitage is a hermit's retreat

explanation.surface: Napoleon's retreat from Moscow became the stuff of history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retreat out of Moscow' conjures Napoleon's army; the retreat is a hermit's HERMITAGE, which loses Moscow's M.
explanation.definitionFit: Heritage is what history hands down to us.
